name: Manasseh
charge: Building again the high places his father destroyed; altars to all the host of heaven in the two courts of the Lord’s house; his children through the fire; observing times, enchantments, witchcraft, familiar spirits and wizards; a carved image in the house of God; Jerusalem filled with innocent blood from one end to another
summary: Manasseh began to reign at twelve and reigned fifty-five years, undoing his father Hezekiah’s reform and leading Judah to do worse than the heathen the Lord had cast out: altars to the host of heaven in the temple courts, his son through the fire, sorcery, a carved image in the house of God, and Jerusalem filled with innocent blood (2 Kings 21:1-16). The captains of Assyria carried him in fetters to Babylon, where he humbled himself and prayed, and the Lord restored him (2 Chronicles 33:11-13). The sentence on the nation stood, and Judah later went into captivity for the sins of Manasseh (2 Kings 24:3-4).
offenseFull: Manasseh was the son of a righteous king whose life the Lord had lengthened, and the people assumed the son must be good too. He was not. He rebuilt the high places Hezekiah had broken down, reared altars for Baal, made a grove as Ahab did, worshipped all the host of heaven, and built altars for them in the two courts of the very house where the Lord had put His name (2 Kings 21:1-5; 2 Chronicles 33:1-5). That is wickedness with zero fear of the Most High. People did not serve idols for nothing but for the self-gratification in it, the same as men keep pagan feasts today for the gifts, the food and the revelling.

He made his son pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom, observed times, used enchantments and witchcraft, and dealt with familiar spirits and wizards (2 Kings 21:6; 2 Chronicles 33:6). Passing a child through the fire is child sacrifice, the same spirit as abortion today, and his own firstborn, the heir to the throne, went in. Every one of these things was a commandment he broke (Deuteronomy 18:10-13). He set a carved image in the house of God (2 Kings 21:7), and seduced Judah to do more evil than the nations the Lord destroyed (2 Kings 21:9). Those nations were driven out for witchcraft, wicked sacrifices, merciless murders of children and feasts of blood (Wisdom of Solomon 12:3-6); we took their land and did the same and worse. How do you become more pagan than the pagans? He also shed very much innocent blood, until Jerusalem was full of it from one end to the other (2 Kings 21:16), and the Lord hates hands that shed innocent blood (Proverbs 6:16-17). The Lord spoke to him and his people through the prophets, and they would not listen (2 Chronicles 33:10).
judgmentFull: The prophets declared that the Lord would bring such evil on Jerusalem that the ears of all who heard of it would tingle, the kind of famine and disease written in the curses (2 Kings 21:10-12). He would stretch over Jerusalem the line of Samaria and the plummet of the house of Ahab: since they worshipped Baal as Ahab did, they would get the same judgment Samaria got from Assyria. He would wipe Jerusalem as a man wipes a dish and turns it upside down, and give the remnant of His inheritance to their enemies as a prey (2 Kings 21:13-15).

In Manasseh’s own day the Lord brought the captains of Assyria, who took him among the thorns, bound him in fetters and carried him to Babylon, then under Assyria (2 Chronicles 33:11). The king they set over themselves was brought into a nation they had not known, as the curse said (Deuteronomy 28:36). In affliction, locked up, his ear was finally opened to discipline, as Job says the Lord does with kings bound in fetters (Job 36:7-10). He humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers and prayed, and the Lord heard him and brought him back to his kingdom; then Manasseh knew that the Lord was God (2 Chronicles 33:12-13). His prayer is written among the sayings of the seers (2 Chronicles 33:18-19), and it is in the Apocrypha, which proves those books belong: he calls on the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob who made heaven and all its host, the very host he had worshipped, and confesses sins above the number of the sands of the sea (Prayer of Manasses 1:1-9). Repentance is not appointed for the just, who keep the law, but for sinners (1 Timothy 1:9).

He showed his repentance in works: he threw the strange gods and the idol out of the house of the Lord, repaired the altar, offered peace offerings and thank offerings, and commanded Judah to serve the Lord (2 Chronicles 33:15-16). This is the pattern of a people called by His name who humble themselves and are heard (2 Chronicles 7:14). Repentance is always possible; our people are repenting, not repented, so no man should judge before the time. Yet the Lord does not forget. Jeremiah, generations later, said Judah would be removed into all kingdoms because of what Manasseh did in Jerusalem (Jeremiah 15:4), and the bands of the Chaldees came in the days of Jehoiakim for his sins and the innocent blood, which the Lord would not pardon (2 Kings 24:2-4). The iniquity was visited on the third and fourth generation.

lawsResolved.text: You shall not engage in idolatry and worship or serve the gods, idols or graven images of other nations.
are commanded to destroy all pagan idols, shrines, alters, groves, pillars, images, etc., that are in the land.
You shall not let any of your offspring pass through the fire of Molech.
A man or a woman with a familiar spirit or who is a wizard shall be put to death.
Divination, soothsaying, and the use of mediums, spiritists and occultists are forbidden practices.
Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.
Confession and repentance necessary to pardon sin and for God to release us from His chastisements and punishments.

text.text: Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and reigned fifty and five years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Hephzi–bah.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, after the abominations of the heathen, whom the Lord cast out before the children of Israel.

For he built up again the high places which Hezekiah his father had destroyed; and he reared up altars for Baal, and made a grove, as did Ahab king of Israel; and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them.
And he built altars in the house of the Lord, of which the Lord said, In Jerusalem will I put my name.
And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord.

And he made his son pass through the fire, and observed times, and used enchantments, and dealt with familiar spirits and wizards: he wrought much wickedness in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.

And he set a graven image of the grove that he had made in the house, of which the Lord said to David, and to Solomon his son, In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all tribes of Israel, will I put my name for ever:

Neither will I make the feet of Israel move any more out of the land which I gave their fathers; only if they will observe to do according to all that I have commanded them, and according to all the law that my servant Moses commanded them.
But they hearkened not: and Manasseh seduced them to do more evil than did the nations whom the Lord destroyed before the children of Israel.
And the Lord spake by his servants the prophets, saying,
Because Manasseh king of Judah hath done these abominations, and hath done wickedly above all that the Amorites did, which were before him, and hath made Judah also to sin with his idols:
Therefore thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Behold, I am bringing such evil upon Jerusalem and Judah, that whosoever heareth of it, both his ears shall tingle.
And I will stretch over Jerusalem the line of Samaria, and the plummet of the house of Ahab: and I will wipe Jerusalem as a man wipeth a dish, wiping it, and turning it upside down.
And I will forsake the remnant of mine inheritance, and deliver them into the hand of their enemies; and they shall become a prey and a spoil to all their enemies;
Because they have done that which was evil in my sight, and have provoked me to anger, since the day their fathers came forth out of Egypt, even unto this day.

Moreover Manasseh shed innocent blood very much, till he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another; beside his sin wherewith he made Judah to sin, in doing that which was evil in the sight of the Lord.
Wherefore the Lord brought upon them the captains of the host of the king of Assyria, which took Manasseh among the thorns, and bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon.
And when he was in affliction, he besought the Lord his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers,
And prayed unto him: and he was intreated of him, and heard his supplication, and brought him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the Lord he was God.
Surely at the commandment of the Lord came this upon Judah, to remove them out of his sight, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he did;
And also for the innocent blood that he shed: for he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood; which the Lord would not pardon.

Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer unto his God, and the words of the seers that spake to him in the name of the Lord God of Israel, behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel.

O Lord, Almighty God of our fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and of their righteous seed;
who hast made heaven and earth, with all the ornament thereof;
who hast bound the sea by the word of thy commandment; who hast shut up the deep, and sealed it by thy terrible and glorious name;
whom all men fear, and tremble before thy power; for the majesty of thy glory cannot be borne, and thine angry threatening toward sinners is importable:
but thy merciful promise is unmeasurable and unsearchable;

for thou art the most high Lord, of great compassion, longsuffering, very merciful, and repentest of the evils of men. Thou, O Lord, according to thy great goodness hast promised repentance and forgiveness to them that have sinned against thee: and of thine infinite mercies hast appointed repentance unto sinners, that they may be saved.

Thou therefore, O Lord, that art the God of the just, hast not appointed repentance to the just, as to Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, which have not sinned against thee; but thou hast appointed repentance unto me that am a sinner:

for I have sinned above the number of the sands of the sea. My transgressions, O Lord, are multiplied: my transgressions are multiplied, and I am not worthy to behold and see the height of heaven for the multitude of mine iniquities.

I am bowed down with many iron bands, that I cannot lift up mine head, neither have any release: for I have provoked thy wrath, and done evil before thee: I did not thy will, neither kept I thy commandments: I have set up abominations, and have multiplied offences.
